terms.meaning: The SI unit of pressure, written Pa. It is the same as a newton per square metre.
The pressure exerted by the air around us.
The calm low-pressure centre that the winds spin around.
A metal rod on a tall building, joined by thick wire to the ground, to carry charge safely down.

items.name: Larger area, lower pressure
items.formula: The same force spread out presses less.
items.example: Broad school bag straps, and a porter’s folded cloth on the head.

items.name: Smaller area, higher pressure
items.formula: The same force on a tiny area presses hard.
items.example: A sharp knife and the point of a nail.

items.name: Liquids press on the walls too
items.formula: A liquid presses on the bottom and the sides of its container.
items.example: Water spurts from a hole in the side of a bottle.

items.name: Pressure and depth
items.formula: Liquid pressure depends on the height of liquid above, not on the width of the vessel.
items.example: Dams are built broader at the base, and water tanks are kept high up.

items.name: Units of air pressure
items.example: A pressure of 1000 mb is 100000 Pa.

items.name: Rubber sucker
items.formula: Pressing it out pushes the air out, and the outside air pressure holds it on.
items.example: This is how a hook with a sucker stays on a smooth wall.

items.name: Why air does not crush us
items.formula: The pressure inside our bodies balances the air pressure outside.
items.example: Blood and other fluids press outward.

items.name: How wind forms
items.formula: Air moves from high pressure to low pressure. Warm air rises and leaves low pressure.
items.example: A bigger pressure difference gives a faster wind.

items.name: Fast wind, low pressure
items.example: Blow between two hanging balloons and they move together. Storms can lift weak roofs.

items.name: Charges in clouds
items.formula: Ice particles and water droplets rub in strong winds, and charges build up.
items.example: Lightning is the sudden flow of these charges.

items.name: Thunder
items.formula: Lightning heats the air so quickly that it expands with a loud sound.
items.example: We see the flash before we hear the sound.

items.name: Local storms in India
items.formula: Kalbaisakhi in West Bengal, Bordoisila in Assam, Mango showers in Kerala and Karnataka.
items.example: These are thunderstorms before the monsoon.

items.name: Safety in lightning
items.formula: Crouch low, away from tall trees. A car or bus is safe.
items.example: Do not hold a metal umbrella.

items.name: How a cyclone forms
items.formula: Warm moist air rises over a warm ocean, leaving very low pressure, and the Earth’s rotation spins the air in.
items.example: A storm surge can flood the coast.

items.name: Tracking cyclones
items.formula: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) follows them using satellites.
items.example: Warnings give people time to reach shelters.

mistakes.text: A wider vessel does not give more pressure at the same depth. Only the height of the liquid counts.
Wind blows from high pressure to low pressure, not the other way.
Do not shelter under a tall lone tree in a thunderstorm.
The eye of a cyclone is calm. The strongest winds are around it, so the danger is not over.
